notes: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate the primary overwintering inoculum of fungal ascospores.
Prune out diseased wood and dead branches at least 15 cm below visible cankers during dry weather; burn or discard infected wood.
Apply systemic myclobutanil or mancozeb at pink bud stage through early summer when cedar galls release orange gelatinous tendrils.
Continue regular seasonal orchard nutrition, soil organic matter additions, and balanced irrigation.
Apply triazole or strobilurin-based fungicides if pustules appear on lower leaves before tasseling and conditions remain humid.
Consider economic threshold spray (e.g., azoxystrobin + propiconazole) if lesions reach the ear leaf at or before silking.
Maintain scheduled side-dress nitrogen applications based on pre-sidedress soil nitrate tests (PSNT).
Prune out and destroy all mummified berries from vines and ground during winter dormancy.
Paint pruning wounds with antifungal sealants or Trichoderma formulations immediately after cutting.
Continue trellis canopy management, leaf pulling around fruiting zones, and pest scouting.
Apply protectant fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb at row closure or when first spots appear on lower leaves.

supplement name: Potato Protective Care: Immediate Fungicide Action
notes: Apply systemic oomycete-targeted compounds (e.g., cymoxanil, mandipropamid, or metalaxyl) immediately upon local blight advisory warning.
Hill soil around stems to protect developing tubers from sunlight (greening) and fungal spores.
Apply fixed copper tank-mixed with mancozeb, which increases soluble copper activity against bacterial strains.

supplement name: Tomato Protective Care: Lower Leaf Pruning
notes: Prune off the bottom 20–30 cm of foliage to eliminate soil-contact splash and increase air circulation.

supplement name: Tomato Protective Care: Immediate Quarantine & Pruning
notes: Bag and cut infected leaves or entire plants in sealed bags immediately. Do not compost.
Apply balanced fertilizer (e.g. NPK 5-10-10 or organic compost) with adequate calcium to prevent blossom end rot.
